asA: test-author writing or amending criteria at DEFINE
iWant: rcf define validate to refuse a new or amended criterion that carries no verification flag
soThat: every criterion a round touches says how it will be verified before BUILD starts
description: The validate rule against a base ref.
title: A test-author cannot add or amend a criterion without its verification flag

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture git repository whose base commit holds US-101 with AC-101-1 (no verification) and whose HEAD adds AC-101-2 with "verification": "external", when rcf define validate --base <base> runs, then it exits 0, prints no "[error]" line, and stderr carries no verification line for AC-101-2.

[failure] Given the same base and a HEAD that adds AC-101-2 with no verification, when rcf define validate --base <base> runs, then it exits 3 with the line "[error] verification AC-101-2 is new since <base7> and carries no verification flag (external | testOnly)".

[failure] Given the same base and a HEAD that changes only the then text of AC-101-1 (still unflagged), when rcf define validate --base <base> runs, then it exits 3 with the line "[error] verification AC-101-1 is amended since <base7> and carries no verification flag (external | testOnly)"; a HEAD that changes only AC-101-1's testable or ownerRef (not description, given, when or then) does not make it amended and validate exits 0.

[edge] Given a fixture project that is not a git repository, or a git repository with no origin/main and no --base, when rcf define validate runs over an unflagged new criterion, then it exits 0 and stderr carries exactly one line "[warn] verification: no base ref; new and amended criteria not checked"; given --base naming a ref that does not resolve it exits 2 with "[error] usage --base <ref> does not resolve".

[must-not] A retired criterion (carrying supersededBy) is never required to carry verification and never appears in the verification report, whether it is new or amended since the base; and the verification rule never changes validate's exit code for any other finding.

[happy] Given this repository's .github/workflows/ci.yml after the slice, when its test job is read, then it checks out with fetch-depth 0, runs "node bin/rcf.js define validate --base origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" from packages/rcf-lite in a step guarded by "if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'", and runs "node bin/rcf.js define validate" with no --base in a step guarded by "if: github.event_name == 'push'", so a push to main never passes an empty base ref.

[happy] Given this repository's .github/workflows/ci.yml after the slice, when its separation job is read, then it runs only on pull_request, checks out the pull request's own head ("ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}") with fetch-depth 0, and runs "node bin/rcf.js audit separation --base origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" from packages/rcf-lite, so the commits it judges are the pull request's own and never the merge commit GitHub synthesises.
